strengths: Genuinely good owned project photography — paver patios, retaining walls, fire pits, pool scapes, outdoor kitchens, plus an owner-with-branded-truck shot. This is the single most valuable asset to carry forward.
Real named client reviews already published on the homepage.
Deep service copy, especially the lawn-health and deck pages, written in a plain, non-corporate voice.
Accessibility toolbar present, and privacy/terms pages already exist.
weaknesses: Zero service-area pages. The site never names Wilkes-Barre, Hazleton, Dallas, or any surrounding town as a landing page, so it competes for nothing outside 'Mountain Top'.
The 5.0 rating across 26 Google reviews appears nowhere above the fold — the strongest trust asset the business owns is invisible until you scroll past the fold into a slider.
No phone number in the header on any page; the only tap-to-call lives in the footer.
Testimonials sit in an auto-rotating carousel that repeats the same three reviews twice.
The 3D-rendering differentiator — the thing that most directly answers homeowner hesitation — is buried in a paragraph on /about rather than being a headline claim.
Heavy all-caps condensed display type in orange-on-white at small sizes hurts legibility.
Hero slider ships four large uncompressed slides; page weight is high on mobile.
carry_forward: All owned project photography (originals recovered from /wp-content/uploads/, not thumbnails)
